moc: Old St Paul's Cathedral: very long Gothic nave with a square crossing tower and NO spire (spire lost 1561), NO dome
Old London Bridge lined with houses
NO Wren dome or Wren steeples

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The men wear long, full-skirted knee-length coats with wide embroidered front borders. They also wear very large full-bottomed wigs, tight knee breeches, white stockings and buckled shoes. The standing man at the right has a sword hanging at his hip.
ghi_chu.ly_do: This silhouette looks like the 1690s–1710s. In 1666 men wore the short Restoration doublet or jacket with petticoat breeches and a shorter, lighter wig. The long coat and vest only came in after the 1666 fashion change, and the full-bottomed wig was not yet common.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The skyline seen through the window shows a dense town with thin pointed Gothic spires. No long Gothic nave with a square crossing tower (Old St Paul's) can be made out. The view is tiny and blurred.
ghi_chu.ly_do: Old St Paul's should dominate the City skyline, with a square crossing tower and no spire. The pointed spires shown do not match that form.
